Living Well / Free resources

Community, access & contribution

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Small ways to contribute attention or skills to shared knowledge, public collections, and community projects.

A meaningful use of technology can benefit someone other than the person operating it. These projects offer ways to help preserve public material, contribute to research, or explore a defined volunteer role. Start by understanding the task and the people it is intended to serve.

Start with: Distributed Proofreaders. Try the public walkthrough before registering or choosing a project.

Volunteer orientation · Free to browse

Smithsonian Transcription Center

Smithsonian Institution

A route into helping public collections become easier to search and read, starting with the project’s own instructions.

Begin here: Read the getting-started instructions, then choose a document and follow the project’s transcription rules.

Access: Public project information is free to browse. Individual contribution workflows may require an account.

Perspective: Museum public participation

By the People

Library of Congress

A small, concrete way to help make historical documents easier for other readers to find and use.

Begin here: Read the introduction and transcription instructions before choosing a page.

Access: The introduction is free. Transcription can be done without registration; reviewing and tracking use an account.

Perspective: Public-library participation

Participatory research · Free to browse

Zooniverse

Zooniverse research teams and volunteers

A way to contribute careful observations to a defined research project rather than simply consuming more information.

Begin here: Choose one project and read its purpose and tutorial before classifying anything.

Access: Projects and tutorials are public. Participation and account requirements depend on the project.

Perspective: Participatory research

Volunteer proofreading · Free account for participation

Distributed Proofreaders

Distributed Proofreaders Foundation

A task that connects close reading with making older books more accessible to other people.

Begin here: Try the public walkthrough before registering or choosing a project.

Access: The walkthrough is public. Register for free to contribute proofreading or other volunteer work.

Perspective: Volunteer preservation of public-domain books

Collaborative mapping · Free to browse

Missing Maps

Missing Maps partner organizations

An example of digital work supporting humanitarian information needs through a shared, reviewable process.

Begin here: Read how the project works, then choose a beginner training route rather than immediately editing.

Access: Free public instructions. Mapping contributions typically need an OpenStreetMap account and training.

Perspective: Humanitarian mapping initiative

Respect privacy and mapping instructions; accuracy and responsible review matter more than contribution volume.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Contribution is not a test of personal worth. Read the instructions, training, privacy rules, and time commitments before joining. A short careful contribution can be more helpful than a large inaccurate one. Opportunities may require registration or selection, and a listing does not guarantee placement or payment.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
